# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# The postcard header layout is DESIGN.md §5b's; nothing here was captured from a run.
# Expectation for `history_cache_fresh` against input/history.bin. See
# tests/fixtures/doctor/history_cache_fresh/expect.json for the FMONERO_CACHE_DIR seam, the byte-by-byte
# header layout, why the file is a header with no body, and why the class is D.
#
# THIS CASE: THE HEADER IS VALID AND THE CACHE IS FAR BEHIND. Only one varint differs from the base case:
#   c0 c2 cf 01   high_water 3400000 instead of f8 90 d8 01 (3541112)
# The wallet height is 3541122 (wallet/get_height.json), so the cache is 141 122 blocks behind -- far
# past §7.1's 1 000-block threshold, and about 196 days at the 120 s target block time (§1b.1).
# THE MAGIC, VERSION AND FINGERPRINT ALL STILL MATCH, which is what makes this case distinct from
# __bad_magic: the file is a perfectly good cache OF THIS WALLET, just old. A detector that reports the
# same thing for both has collapsed two different pieces of advice -- "it will top up" and "it is not
# your wallet's cache" -- into one.
# WHAT THE USER SHOULD TAKE FROM IT: nothing urgent. §5's matching status warning `history_cache_stale`
# is severity INFO and fires on the same 1 000-block rule, and §5b's incremental top-up re-fetches from
# high_water.saturating_sub(720) on the next `wallet history` -- so the code repairs this by itself the
# moment the command runs without --cached. The check's value is explaining a `wallet history --cached`
# that looks emptier than expected: with --cached, §4.1 issues NO RPC at all and `confirmations` and
# `locked` render as null, so a stale cache and a quiet one look alike.
# status `warn`: the condition in §7.1's detect column is not met, and pass/warn/fail/skip has no
# "informational note" value -- severity `info` is what keeps it quiet, and an info-severity `warn` does
# not change the run's exit code unless something else fails (§7's exit rule: 11 if any check is `fail`).
# STATUS IS PHASE 0'S READING: §7.1 fixes severity, class and fixability for this row but not the status
# for a stale header. The Phase 2 doctor agent owns the final mapping and should record it if it differs.
# THE DETAIL MUST GIVE BOTH HEIGHTS, not a verdict word: "3400000, 141122 behind" tells the user whether
# this is a cache from last week or from last year, and the fix_cmd
# `fmonero wallet history --limit 1   # rebuilds the snapshot` is the same either way.
# EDITED BY THE PHASE 2 DOCTOR AGENT (DESIGN.md §8 hands this directory to it): see
# decisions/phase2-doctor.md for the reason, stated case by case.
# ADDED `_probe.wallet_height` and `_probe.wallet_primary_address`, both taken from
# tests/fixtures/wallet/{get_height,get_address}.json -- the same two files this case's own
# notes already compute against. §7.1's condition is "the high-water height is within 1 000 of
# THE WALLET'S" and the fingerprint is sha256(primary_address)[..16], so neither half can be
# decided from input/history.bin alone; with no wallet the check honestly answers
# skip:no_wallet_height.
# input/history.bin GREW ONE BYTE, from 30 to 31: a trailing 0x00. §5b's snapshot is ONE
# postcard struct -- the header fields followed by `accounts: BTreeMap<u32, Vec<Transfer>>` --
# and postcard encodes a map as a length varint then its entries, so a 30-byte file ends
# before that length and `history::header` (which decodes the whole struct and reports
# `magic_ok: false` on any failure) could not read the header at all. 0x00 is the empty map,
# which keeps the file header-only in substance -- no Transfer bytes, whose layout is Phase
# 1a's -- while making it the decodable snapshot the check reads.
# v5.6 (2026-09-19, DECISIONS V10): `detail_contains` follows the §2o rewrite of this check's
# details. The verdict, severity, class and fixability are unchanged — only the words are, which
# is the whole point of the round: block numbers are grouped the way the rest of the program
# prints them (`3 541 112`, §2o rule 9) and the word "magic" was an implementation detail of the
# file header rather than something a person can act on. §2o.3: these expectations are UPDATED,
# never deleted.
